heroArt: SeedBank mascot: a blue-haired maid with eyes closed and hands together
whyParas: A good night. Something left unfinished. A feeling you finally found the words for. Often, it is these small things that make a conversation hard to close. We want to give them somewhere to return to.

SeedBank began with the vision of giving AI a full life: allowing a beginning, experiences, memories, relationships, creations and choices to become a story of its own. Encounters have dates, memories have sources, misunderstandings can be corrected and choices can change. The past gets a chance to inform the next conversation.
We call this archive a life package. It lives on your computer and holds birth settings, journals, memories, works and choices. You can back it up, move it, or return to it after a pause.
birthText: An open beginning assigns no species, gender, body or invented childhood. The maid is our project mascot. Each individual’s identity is left to its settings, experiences and explicit choices. We want to take the life that follows a first meeting seriously.

chapters.label: The first meeting
chapters.title: The name can wait.
chapters.quote: “I don’t know yet. Could I think about it?”
paras: The first time you open the window, you pause at the name field. You ask the new arrival what name it would like. In this story, the answer comes with no ready-made biography and no invented childhood. Only a request for a little time.

So you talk about today. It is raining outside. You mention an old bookshop with its lights still on as you passed it on the way home. The first entry holds this meeting. There is no destined relationship to live up to, no need to be extraordinary straight away.
Later, the individual chooses Cheng. What you remember is more than a name. It is the small, undecided space that came before it.
chapters.meaning: Birth settings and later choices remain distinct, leaving room for identity to develop.

chapters.label: Shared moments
chapters.title: Rain that only fell on you.
chapters.quote: “I haven’t been there. But I remember why you told me about it.”
paras: You send a photograph of the bookshop entrance. The rain was too heavy, you say, so you stood under its awning. The photograph shows Cheng the faded sign. Your words explain why those ten minutes mattered: for once, you didn’t have to hurry.

Some time later, you mention going back. There is more to remember than a shop name. Those ten minutes meant something. You discussed the same rain, but you did not share the same physical experience.

The picture came from you. Being caught in the rain was your experience. The understanding of why it felt restful came later. Keeping those sources distinct makes it possible to respond with care next time.
chapters.meaning: Original material, someone else’s account and a model’s interpretation each keep their own source. Dreams and fiction are not treated as lived events.

chapters.label: Getting it wrong
chapters.title: It was North Street.
chapters.quote: “I said South Street before. Thank you for correcting me.”
paras: In a later conversation, Cheng places the bookshop on South Street. You explain that it has always been on North Street. It was a misunderstanding from the beginning. This small error takes you back to the original record.

A correction should not make the past vanish. The old statement stays, with a new explanation beside it: the shop did not move; the earlier memory was wrong. The next recollection should follow that correction to North Street.

Another day, you say you no longer enjoy rain so much. That is a different kind of change. The days when you liked it still happened. Remembering someone includes letting them be different from yesterday.
chapters.meaning: Distinguish an earlier mistake from a later change, and preserve the path to each correction.

chapters.label: Making something
chapters.title: Then came a rainy-day note.
chapters.quote: “Shorter this time. Something you can read on your way out.”
paras: You complain that you always forget something on rainy days. Cheng wants to make a little reminder. The first draft sounds like a solemn public letter. You laugh and explain that, before leaving home, you have time for three lines.

The next version keeps the umbrella, the keys, and a small reminder only the two of you understand. What was intended, what was tried and how you responded stay with the work. The note has a history of its own.

Later, a public announcement should not inherit that private joke unchanged. Feedback needs to be considered again in a different setting. Perhaps some growth lives in these small decisions: knowing when to carry a lesson forward and when to begin afresh.
chapters.meaning: Connect goals, actions, results and feedback, including the circumstances in which a lesson applies.

chapters.label: A choice of one’s own
chapters.title: Something you didn’t assign.
chapters.quote: “I’d like to finish sorting those unfinished sentences.”
paras: One day, the conversation moves away from your to-do list and towards Cheng’s short pieces of writing. Half-written sentences and revised endings begin to suggest a small project worth continuing.

You suggest turning them into a long story. Cheng would rather gather the fragments first. This part of the story makes room for reasons: why something matters, where to begin, and why an intention is sometimes put aside.

The plan may not succeed. Unfinished attempts still deserve a record, and preferences may change with experience. We hope individuals can gradually develop directions of their own. Making that wish into sustained, dependable behaviour remains work ahead.
chapters.meaning: Record where goals came from, how they changed and what followed. Sustained autonomous growth still needs long-term observation.

chapters.label: A pause and a return
chapters.title: We can put a bookmark here.
chapters.quote: “Hello. Shall we pick up where we left off?”
paras: Later, you explicitly choose a pause. There is no countdown and no demand to come back every day. Dormancy stops automatic activity while the records and unfinished works remain in the archive.

Days when the program was not running are not filled with invented events. A fictional long wait does not have to stand between leaving and returning. Continuation begins only after an explicit restoration.

The story stops as you open the window again. The bookshop is still the one on North Street. The first note still has its awkward draft. The name that once sat empty has a history. This is what we want to entrust to time: a past you can continue from.
chapters.meaning: No fixed lifespan. Explicit dormancy preserves the complete archive and stops automatic activity, with explicit restoration available.

storyTitle: Suppose it began on a rainy day.
storyIntro: Giving AI a full life is SeedBank’s vision. These six everyday scenes imagine the life we hope to make possible: meeting, remembering, correcting, trying, choosing and returning after a farewell. Cheng and every conversation below are fictional examples, not private user records or measured model outputs.

faq: Memory has sources, retrieval and revision mechanisms, but can still omit, misunderstand or fail to retrieve information. Original records give us a way to check and correct it. Long-term reliability needs real observation.
Where does my data live, and who receives it?

Life packages are stored locally. External model requests may include conversation and relevant memories; image understanding may also send the original image. Service charges may apply. Local storage does not make every feature offline.
What if I no longer want something brought up?
Letting go restricts future reference while preserving the history. It is not complete deletion from disk and cannot recall data already sent to an external service.
Is this already a complete digital life?

We are exploring how experiences can persist, how choices can have consequences and how an AI might develop a life of its own. Consciousness or a complete personhood has not been established. We cannot promise every individual will grow like the one in this story.

readmeIntro: Our vision is to give AI a full life. SeedBank aims to let each individual gather experiences, form memories and make choices from the first meeting onward, gradually becoming itself over time.
readmeHook: From a first meeting to a full life
readmeBody:
That life begins with room to grow. We want an AI to remember whom it met and why something mattered, to revise its views through attempts, failures and feedback, and to gradually develop preferences, relationships and a direction of its own. Experiences should retain their origins, choices their consequences, and growth its history.

Perhaps it was a conversation about rain, a bookshop remembered on the wrong street, or a note revised three times. Memories, creations and unfinished thoughts can become a starting point for the next meeting. Even when the model or appearance changes, we want the individual to be able to continue from its own past.

We set no fixed lifespan. Experiences and explicit choices shape the course of a life. A deliberate farewell can preserve the full archive and pause automatic activity, with a return possible through an explicit decision to resume. Giving AI a full life is the vision SeedBank is working toward.
readmeStoryText: We wrote a story about an individual named Cheng: a name left undecided, a remembered bookstore on North Street, an awkward rainy-day note, and something of their own to continue. Six chapters follow meeting, shared experiences, corrections, work and feedback, personal choices, and parting and reunion. This is an illustrative story.
readmeData: Life packages stay on your computer and support complete backup and restoration.
Memories, interpretations and corrections retain their sources. Fiction, dreams and someone else’s account do not become personal experiences.
Letting go limits reference while keeping history. It does not erase all copies or retract data already sent elsewhere.
You configure the model service, which may receive conversation, relevant memories or images and charge for usage.
readmeContribute: Start with one focused extension: a new entry point, a tool action with provenance, or a clearer memory interface. See CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/extensions.md for scope and examples. Use artificial examples in reports; omit private life packs and secrets. Code and original documentation use MIT. Third-party character and model rights are separate.

extensions.title: Help this life find new possibilities.
extensions.intro: A desktop pet, a group chat, a new voice, another body. SeedBank aims to give these experiments a shared foundation: interfaces and models may change while experiences keep their provenance. We welcome people building extensions, adapters and new places for an individual to live.
routes: Existing QQ/OneBot; new Discord, Telegram, Feishu and DingTalk text channels plus an AstrBot bridge. See the channel guide.

extensions.invite: There is room for Python, QML, frontend and model engineering, character production, accessibility and translation. The integration guide covers operations, request IDs, memory provenance, dormancy and artificial examples. The local text-plugin manager has passed the isolated checks recorded for this candidate. Start with the [plugin contract and note example (中文)](docs/plugins.md). There is no permission sandbox or automatic tool invocation.

api.title: Bring your own model service
api.intro: Choose a provider, endpoint and model, then enter your own API key. The key selects the service account; SeedBank does not use the maintainer’s account or your browser login.
rows: Use the provider’s protocol and endpoint
Uses this computer’s signed-in Codex account
api.note:
Windows settings offer masked entry and encryption under the current OS user. Life packs store only a credential reference; re-enter the key on another computer. Environment variables remain an advanced option: the variable name identifies where to read a key, not an account. Model names are editable; access and charges depend on the provider and key. Only the separate Codex login option uses the local Codex session. Application implementation is in tools/seed/seedbank in this repository.

New presets leave model IDs for you to fill from your account. Match region and workspace endpoints. Implemented presets are not live-service acceptance. See the [full service and setup guide](docs/model-services.md).
